parts:

it nearly always crashes on the second function call, sometimes on the first and sometimes completes both.

If the same code is simply run without the enclosing R function it always runs OK.   
My only thought was the very low value of warmup which I used,  is there a lower limit ?

Thanks in advance

Ashley Ford

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: rstan partialy reproducible Segmentation fault (core dumped)
parts:
On Tuesday, July 21, 2015 at 2:02:52 PM UTC-4, Ashley Ford wrote:
In what I hoped was a simple test example I get a segmentation fault from the code in the attached file
it nearly always crashes on the second function call, sometimes on the first and sometimes completes both.

Thanks for reporting. Until we get this fixed for real, you can work around the problem by assigning the output to an object in R's global environment, like

posterior <- stan.Himellblau()

and subsequent calls to stan.Himellblau() work (for me) as long as posterior is not removed.

Ben
